title: Kholak (Tsampa with Butter Tea)
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (roasted barley flour, butter tea, salt). Use cow butter instead of yak butter if preferred. Chhang variation is optional - omit for Jain version.
description: The ultimate quick Ladakhi breakfast of roasted barley flour (tsampa/namphey) mixed into salty butter tea (gur gur chai) and kneaded into a soft dough or porridge. Highly nutritious, portable, and ideal for high-altitude life.
ingredients: 1–2 cups hot butter tea (or plain salted tea)
1–2 tsp yak or cow butter (optional extra)
steps: Prepare or heat salted butter tea.
Place tsampa in a bowl, pour a little hot butter tea over it.
Mix and knead with fingers into a soft dough or thicker porridge consistency.
Eat as is, or with a little extra butter.
tips: Traditionally eaten any time of day; perfect trekking food.
Can be made with water or diluted chhang in some valleys for variation.

title: Khambir (Tagi) with Butter Tea
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (whole wheat flour, yeast/starter, salt, butter tea). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables.
description: Traditional Ladakhi whole-wheat sourdough flatbread, slightly sour and dense, baked on a hot stone then over open fire. Staple breakfast bread served with gur gur chai (butter tea).
steps: Knead flour, yeast/starter, salt and water into a soft dough. Ferment overnight or several hours.
Shape into thick rounds.
Bake first on a hot stone or pan, then finish directly over low fire or coals for a firm crust.
Serve warm with butter tea, apricot jam, or plain butter.
tips: Keeps well for several days at room temperature.
Symbol of hospitality in Ladakhi homes.

title: Paba
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (mixed roasted flours, ghee/butter, salt). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables.
description: Dense multi-grain bread or pudding made from roasted barley, peas, wheat or buckwheat flour mixed with boiling water. Slathered with ghee and eaten with vegetables or dal.
steps: Mix the roasted flours with salt.
Pour boiling water and stir vigorously into a thick dough or soft pudding consistency.
Shape into a loaf or serve as is.
Serve hot with ghee and simple vegetables or lentils.
tips: Highly sustaining field food traditionally carried to work.

title: Vegetable Skyu
jainNotes: Contains root vegetables (carrots, turnips, potatoes) - not consumed by Jains.
description: Iconic Ladakhi one-pot stew of hand-shaped thumbprint wheat pasta cooked with root vegetables in a mild broth. True local dish (not purely Tibetan).
ingredients: Onion, ginger (optional traditional use is minimal)
Salt, black pepper, fresh herbs (cilantro, celery greens)
steps: Knead firm dough, roll into ropes, pinch into small ear/shell shapes.
Sauté aromatics lightly if using, add vegetables and water/broth.
Simmer until vegetables soften, then add pasta pieces.
Cook until pasta is tender. Adjust seasoning and serve hot.
tips: Sometimes made with milk (oma-skyu) for creamier version.
Root vegetables are traditional; omit for stricter diets.

title: Chutagi (Chhutagi)
jainNotes: Contains root vegetables (carrots, turnips, potatoes) - not consumed by Jains.
description: 'Water bread' – bow-tie or ear-shaped whole-wheat pasta cooked in a hearty vegetable broth. Festive yet everyday Ladakhi pasta stew.
ingredients: Carrots, turnips, potatoes, peas, spinach or local greens
steps: Make dough, roll out, cut into circles then pinch into bow-tie shapes.
Prepare vegetable broth with chopped roots and greens.
Add pasta shapes and simmer until cooked through.
Serve piping hot.
tips: Often prepared during harvest season for energy.
Meat version with goat trotters exists for non-veg.

title: Vegetable Thukpa
jainNotes: Contains onion, ginger, garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.
description: Clear noodle soup of Tibetan origin fully adopted in Ladakh. Hand-pulled or cut wheat/barley noodles in a light vegetable broth with local greens.
ingredients: Wheat or barley noodles (fresh or dried)
Carrots, cabbage, spinach or local greens
steps: Prepare clear vegetable broth.
Add chopped vegetables and simmer.
Cook noodles separately or in the broth until tender.
Season and garnish with fresh herbs. Serve hot.
tips: Variants include thenthuk (hand-pulled) and gyathuk.
Widely available in Leh restaurants in both veg and non-veg forms.

title: Mutton Skyu
jainNotes: Contains mutton and onion - not consumed by Jains.
description: Hearty version of the classic Ladakhi pasta stew cooked with mutton or bone broth, root vegetables and hand-shaped wheat pieces.
steps: Pressure-cook or simmer mutton until tender; reserve broth.
Shape dough into small ear-shaped pieces.
Add vegetables and pasta to the broth and cook until done.
Return meat and adjust seasoning.
tips: Ideal winter dish for warmth and calories.

title: Vegetable Momos (Mokmok)
jainNotes: Contains onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.
description: Steamed dumplings of Tibetan origin, now a Ladakhi staple. Thin wheat wrappers filled with mixed vegetables, served with chilli chutney or clear soup.
ingredients: Cabbage, carrot, onion, spinach or local greens
steps: Knead soft dough and rest.
Finely chop and season vegetable filling.
Roll thin circles, fill, and pleat into half-moon or round shapes.
Steam 12–15 minutes until cooked. Serve with spicy tomato-chilli chutney.
tips: Mokthuk is the version served in soup.

title: Mutton Momos
jainNotes: Contains mutton and onion - not consumed by Jains.
description: Classic meat-filled steamed dumplings popular across Ladakh. Minced mutton or lamb seasoned simply, wrapped and steamed.
ingredients: Salt, black pepper, a little oil
steps: Prepare dough and rest.
Mix minced meat with finely chopped aromatics and seasoning.
Fill and pleat dumplings.
Steam until fully cooked (about 15 minutes). Serve with chilli sauce.
tips: Yak meat was traditional but is now restricted; mutton is the common substitute.

title: Yarkhandi Pulao
jainNotes: Contains mutton and onion - not consumed by Jains.
description: Festive, rich rice dish brought via the Silk Route by Yarkhandi traders. Slow-cooked mutton with rice, dried fruits, nuts and animal fat – once considered haute cuisine of Ladakh.
ingredients: Raisins, apricot kernels or dried apricots
steps: Slow-cook mutton until very tender.
Fry carrots, nuts and dried fruits in ghee.
Layer or mix with soaked rice and the meat broth.
Cook until rice is done and flavours meld. Serve with clear soup on the side.
tips: Rice was historically a luxury grain in the region.
Modern versions are less fatty than the traditional ones.

title: Tingmo (Timok) with Vegetable Stew
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic in the vegetable stew - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, serve with Jain-friendly stew (no onion-garlic).
description: Soft steamed Tibetan-style leavened buns popular in Ladakh, usually eaten with a simple vegetable or meat stew or dal.
ingredients: Vegetable stew or dal for serving (contains onion, garlic)
steps: Prepare soft yeasted dough and proof.
Shape into flower-like or round steamed buns.
Steam 15–20 minutes until fluffy.
Serve hot with stew or dal.
tips: Also eaten as a snack or with butter tea.

title: Steamed Vegetable Momos
jainNotes: Contains onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.
description: Smaller portion of vegetable momos commonly sold as street or café snack throughout Leh and Ladakh towns.
ingredients: Cabbage, carrot, onion, spinach or local greens
steps: Knead soft dough and rest.
Finely chop and season vegetable filling.
Roll thin circles, fill, and pleat into half-moon or round shapes.
Steam 12–15 minutes until cooked. Serve with spicy tomato-chilli chutney.
tips: Ubiquitous snack; also available fried or in soup (mokthuk).

title: Khambir (Snack)
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (whole wheat flour, yeast/starter, salt). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables.
description: Thick sourdough Ladakhi bread torn and eaten plain, with butter, apricot jam, or local cheese as a simple anytime snack.
steps: Knead flour, yeast/starter, salt and water into a soft dough. Ferment overnight or several hours.
Shape into thick rounds.
Bake first on a hot stone or pan, then finish directly over low fire or coals for a firm crust.
Serve at room temperature or lightly warmed with butter, jam, or cheese.
tips: Keeps for days; ideal travel food.

title: Gur Gur Chai (Butter Tea)
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (tea, butter, salt). Use cow butter instead of yak butter if preferred.
description: Salty yak-butter tea churned until frothy. More than a drink – a daily high-calorie staple and cultural ritual of Ladakh and the wider Himalayan region.
ingredients: Strong black or green tea leaves
steps: Brew strong tea concentrate.
Add salt and butter.
Churn vigorously in a dongmo (traditional churn) or modern blender until emulsified and frothy.
Serve hot in small bowls.
tips: Acquired taste for most outsiders; essential for hydration and warmth at altitude.
Often drunk throughout the day with khambir or tsampa.
